annotationRationale: The method enumerates all successful square-type histories, multiplies their successive conditional transition probabilities, and adds the probabilities of the disjoint histories. Equally likely hop directions supply the individual transition probabilities.
sourceMethod: Follows the official first solution using center, edge, and corner types. It explains the transition probabilities and why exactly four successful type sequences are possible.

review.mathCheck: From every noncorner edge square, the transition probabilities to corner, center, and edge are respectively 1/2, 1/4, and 1/4. The exhaustive first-corner histories mec, meec, memec, and meeec have probabilities 1/2, 1/8, 1/8, and 1/32. Their sum is 25/32, confirming D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully adapts the first MAA Solution 23 on page 16, using the same four square-type histories. Original prose adds explicit transition, exhaustiveness, and disjointness justifications. The alternative matrix method is not needed.
review.annotationCheck: Wrap-around moves, stopping at the first corner, and the four-hop limit are handled correctly. The grouped histories need not be equally likely. The explanation is reconstructible at AMC 12 level.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The multiplication link is an accepted partial crosswalk: successive conditional probabilities are multiplied with positive conditioning probabilities; zero-probability handling is untested. The addition link supports disjoint-event summation, without demonstrating non-disjoint inclusion-exclusion. cnm_285 appropriately supports counting equally likely directions.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.8 applies through the underlying uniform direction choices, despite unequal grouped-history probabilities. S-CP.B.7 is exercised in its disjoint case only. The accepted partial 7.SP.C.7a link supports direction-count probabilities; independent construction of a uniform model is not demonstrated.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_h245 and cnm_h138 correctly identify the assessed conditional multiplication and disjoint addition. cnm_285 is appropriate background for the individual transition probabilities.
